Health Domain - Public Health and Governance Regulations

Public health activities are governed by public health laws, CDC guidelines (in US), WHO recommendations, and HIPAA's public health exception (45 CFR 164.512(b)).

For Disease Surveillance: Required attributes include case identifier (may be anonymized), disease diagnosis, diagnosis date, reporting entity, location (aggregated to protect privacy), age group, gender (for epidemiology), and vaccination status if relevant. Patient name is NOT required - de-identified data is preferred for surveillance. Contact information required only for follow-up investigations.

For Immunization Management: Required attributes include individual identifier (name and DOB), vaccine type and lot number, vaccination date, vaccination site, healthcare provider identifier, and adverse event reporting if applicable. For children, parent/guardian information required. Insurance information for billing.

For Epidemic Monitoring: Required attributes include case counts (aggregated), geographic location (county/state level), time period, age demographics (aggregated), and risk factors (aggregated). Individual patient identifiers are NOT required for epidemic monitoring - only aggregated data. Contact information required only for contact tracing.

For Public Health Reporting: Required attributes include report type (notifiable disease, outbreak, etc.), reporting entity, report date, aggregate data (case counts, demographics), and required data elements per regulation. Patient identifiers NOT required unless mandated by specific reporting requirements (e.g., certain infectious diseases).

For Health Program Evaluation: Required attributes include program identifier, participant identifiers (may be anonymized), participation dates, outcome measures, and aggregate statistics. Individual-level data may be anonymized or aggregated. Contact information only if follow-up required.

UNNECESSARY Attributes: Religion is unnecessary unless for minority health programs with legal authorization. Political affiliation is never required. Full address is unnecessary if location is aggregated.

HIPAA Public Health Exception (45 CFR 164.512(b)): Permits disclosure of PHI to public health authorities for surveillance, reporting, and prevention activities without individual authorization.

Data Minimization: Public health activities should use de-identified or aggregated data when possible. Individual identifiers only when necessary for follow-up or contact tracing.
